fields.meta_title: Gmail Automation for Invoices, Leads, and Support | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build Gmail automation that reads invoice emails into records, routes leads, follows up on quotes, and escalates unanswered support email.
fields.h1: Build Gmail Automation That Goes Past Filters
fields.hero_description: Build Gmail automation that turns each incoming email into a record, an owner, and a deadline in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the App Does With Each Email
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the whole Gmail workflow from one prompt, including its records and the screen your team works from.
fields.feature_1:
Starts the moment an email lands

Connects to your Gmail account through its API. A new message from a supplier, a lead or a customer starts the run, and the app sorts it by sender, subject, and the words inside.
fields.feature_2:
Reads attachments into fields

An AI step turns an attached invoice or receipt into fields such as vendor, amount, and due date. Any value the AI is unsure of goes to a person to confirm before the record saves.
fields.feature_3:
Gives every email an owner

You write the routing rules: team size, product, region, or the sender domain. The app sends each email to the right person by Slack or email alert and records who has it.
fields.feature_4:
Chases the replies that never came

Set how many days a sent quote or request can sit without an answer. The app sends a follow-up from your own address in the same thread, then alerts you if that goes quiet too.
fields.feature_5:
Keeps every thread in your database

Each email the app handles becomes a row with its sender, its status, and the person who owns it. The data sits in a database you own, and there is no cap on the tasks it runs.
fields.feature_6:
Your Gmail app's code, in GitHub

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can read every routing rule and API call, and change how the app treats a sender without starting over.

fields.tab_content_1:
Dagny signs off on any field under 90%

Supplier invoices reach Hollinshead Joinery as attachments in the accounts inbox. The app reads INV-4471 from Ferrovale Timber into vendor, total, and due date. Any field read under 90% confidence waits for bookkeeper Dagny Lowenfeld, and the due date is one. Once she confirms it, the $2,840.00 bill is saved.
fields.tab_content_2:
Teams of 10 or more reach sales the same hour

Saoirse Valdane emails Marlowgate Coworking's sales inbox about desks for her team of 14. The app saves her company, team size, and start month to a new lead. Any inquiry for 10 or more people goes to sales lead Tobiah Renquist by Slack direct message. Smaller teams stay in the sales inbox.
fields.tab_content_3:
Unanswered after 3 days means a second email

Yusra Pembleton sends quote Q-2318 for $6,450 to Pennacrest Dental from her Gmail account, and the app logs it against the thread. With no reply after 3 days, the app sends a short follow-up from her account in the same thread. If 7 days pass with nothing back, the quote is marked cold and Yusra gets an alert.
fields.tab_content_4:
After 4 quiet hours, Ruairi gets the ticket

Each email to Cobblefield Bike Hire's support address gets an automatic reply with a ticket number. Ticket #5126, about a bike lock that will not open, has had no answer for 4 hours. Any ticket quiet that long goes to support lead Ruairi Delacroix by Slack direct message, with the customer's email attached.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up Gmail automation for one inbox, test it on real mail, and then move on to the next inbox.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the inbox that eats the most time
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Note what happens to each email
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Connect Gmail and your other tools
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the numbers each rule uses
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the shared addresses and personal inboxes your team reads each day, such as accounts, sales, and support. Count a normal week of mail in each. Start with the inbox where a person retypes email into another system, because that is where errors and delays pile up.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Take ten recent emails from that inbox and note what a person did with each one: where the details went, who got told, and what reply went back. Those notes become the rules. An email nobody acted on belongs in a filter, not an app.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give the app access to the Gmail account through its API, along with the tools the email ends up in: your accounting system, CRM, or ticket list. Use a shared address for team inboxes, so the workflow does not depend on one person's login.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Every rule needs a number someone agreed to: the confidence below which a person checks an extracted field, the team size that counts as a large lead, the days before a follow-up, the hours before an escalation. Write them down before you build.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the workflow in a prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent which inbox to watch, what to pull from each email, where to save it, and who hears about the exceptions. Emergent builds the workflow, its database, and a dashboard. You change any rule later by prompting, without starting over.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write five emails from a second account that match the cases in your notes, including one that should go to a person. Check that each one lands on the right record, that the reply reads well, and that the alert reaches the person you named.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Review the hand-offs for two weeks
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read every email the app passed to a person and every one it handled alone. Where it handed off something your records could answer, add that rule by prompting. When the hand-offs settle, move to the next inbox on your list.

plan.angle: The top 10 are listicles of Gmail add-ons, a YouTube Apps Script tutorial and tool vendors, and the AI Overview sorts the answer into filters, Workspace features and connector platforms. This page starts where filters stop: four inboxes where an email has to become work in another system (an invoice in the books, a lead with an owner, a quote that gets chased, a support email with a deadline), each with its trigger, its rule and the person who hears about it, connected to the user's own Gmail account through its API.
tab_stories: Thistlebrook Joinery's accounts inbox gets invoice INV-4471 from Calderwood Timber; the app reads the attached invoice into fields, and because the due date reads at 72% confidence, under the 90% bar, bookkeeper Ines Varga checks it before the $2,840.00 bill is saved.

Fernvale Coworking's sales inbox gets an inquiry from Odile Marchetti for a team of 14; the app saves company, team size and start month to the lead record, and any team of 10 or more goes to sales lead Bram Okafor by Slack direct message.
Quote Q-2318 for $6,450 goes to Halvorsen Dental from Petra Lindqvist's Gmail; with no reply after 3 days, the app sends a follow-up from her account in the same thread and logs it on the quote.

Wrenmoor Bike Hire's support inbox answers each new email with a ticket number; ticket #5126 about a broken lock has gone 4 hours without a reply, so the app sends support lead Callum Achterberg a Slack direct message.
